newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian gold explorers "rocked" by Busang fraud.
newsitem.headline: Australian gold explorers "rocked" by Busang fraud.

text.p: The Australian mining industry reacted with shock and disbelief on Monday to news that Indonesia's fabled Busang gold deposit was a hoax.
The Association of Mining and Exploration Companies, which represents many of Australia's listed gold companies, said the Busang saga would shake confidence in the entire gold industry.
"The whole industry is in a state of shock at what happened," said association chief executive George Savell.
"It will rock confidence for a while, but this is a very, very big industry and this is a very isolated incident."
Earlier, independent analyst Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd said it believed core samples from the Busang area were tampered with and assay results falsified on an unprecedented scale.
An economic deposit could not be found, it said in a report to Canadian gold prospector Bre-X Minerals. Bre-X claimed to have discovered a 71-million-ounce mother lode.
Savell said he did not believe the disappointment of Busang would lead to changes in the way samples are handled and verified in Australia, but a review was likely.
"The industry will also have a very, very good look at the way it does things," he told Reuters from Perth.
"It will certainly review what it does to make sure there aren't any loopholes to be used, but there's always the possibility at a remote site to fool with samples."
He said Australian gold prospectors and miners were shocked when Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc first raised doubts about Busang early this year.
Freeport made its own assessment of Busang during due diligence on a deal to buy 15 percent of the Busang property.
"I think there will be a very short-term effect because the Australian industry has a very, very good reputation. They are not a bunch of cowboys," Savell said.
